TRAINING:Training has been very fun and intense. Lots of technical, sparring and cardio training. 

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training when I was 15 years old. I was smaller in high school and didn’t grow until later, so when I saw the early UFCs with Royce Gracie I wanted to train in BJJ and MMA.

What ranks and titles have you held? Black belt Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, 2nd deg black belt Pancrase MMA/Jiu-Jitsu. 7 times King of Pancrase/ 1st middleweight King of Pancrase/ Pancrase 2002 Spirit Tour Champion, Pancrase Trans Tournament Champion/ Bas Rutten Invitational Middleweight Tournament Champion, Ring of Fire Middleweight Champion/ I.M.A. Rumble in the Rockies Tournament Champion, Strikeforce welterweight champion

Do you have any heroes? Jesus Christ.

What is your favorite technique? The Marquardt Choke.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? I am fulfilling my dreams and my destiny.  It is something I have looked forward to since I was a 100 lb 15 year old.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went for two years but I left everything behind to go train in Japan.

What was your job before you started fighting? Desk job for the phone company. It really sucked!

TRAINING: I start training with the fight team at noon every weekday. Our training varies from standup, wrestling, and jiu-jitsu, with sparring and technique work daily. In the evening, I get my cardio in at the Combat Circuit training facility at the AKA. Every other day, I hit mitts with my standup coach, Andy Fong.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started training MMA at Purdue during the off season as a way to stay in shape and expand my skills as a wrestler. I fell in love with the sport and by the time I had graduated, I already had two amateur fights under my belt. It started as a hobby, and turned into my passion and full time job.

What ranks and titles have you held? Two-time Indiana wrestling state champion, junior national freestyle champion, three-time NCAA tournament qualifier, top 10 career wins at Purdue University, Purdue wrestling team captain

Do you have any heroes? My parents that did everything it took to raise their three boys, Cain Velasquez, and Herschel Walker

What does it mean for you to fight in STRIKEFORCE? It is a great opportunity and an honor to fight for one of the best organizations in the world. I'm so thankful for the chance to showcase my skills on such a grand stage alongside some of the greatest martial artists in the world.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started MMA when I was 14 years old. It was the first combat sport I tried, and I took to it straight away! I’ve never looked back since. I suppose I started because I was a pretty small kid, and I felt the need early on in life to learn how to defend myself. I was always aware of conflict and situations where it could arise, and I wanted to feel I could handle myself when the circumstances arose.

What professional titles have you held? I don’t currently hold any titles in MMA - I’m waiting for the UFC world title to be my first.

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? As an amateur. I won multiple titles like the Cage Warriors Academy title and the European Cage Warriors Grand Prix, which earned me a pro contract with the promotion!

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? I’m currently a BJJ brown belt working towards my black!

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? My toughest fight to date would have to be my fight Michele Martignoni back in 2021. At the time he was undefeated, 6-0, and since has gone on to win Cage Warriors gold. I finished him in the third round with a rear naked choke after a back-and-forth battle. What made this fight so tough, though, was that on fight day I woke up so ill with food poisoning and still managed to battle through 3 rounds and earn a submission victory late in the fight! This, along with other obstacles I’ve overcome, has helped forge my bombproof mindset towards competing.

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Hard to pick a favorite because there’s so many I respect for so many different reasons. Growing up, I always looked up to Urijah Faber, as he paved the way for the lighter weight class guys. He was a trail blazer. I also am a big fan of Alexander Volkanovski. Well-rounded, world class gas tank, and seems like a sick bloke.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I never went to college. As soon as I finished school I worked a few s**tty jobs and pursued fighting. I’ve always known this is what I wanted to do.

What was your job before you started fighting? I worked as a janitor in a church / fitness centre for a few months. I also waited tables for a bit and worked in a retail store. All were just a means to an end to fund my training.

Personal Life/Background: I live with my brothers, George and Harvey, and our dad Andrew. I have a little sister who lives with my mum. I have an amazing girlfriend called Priya, who’s been with me since the start, literally the last 10 years (we met when we were in school). I have a few real close friends, and then there’s the boys in the gym. I keep my circle small and I’m chasing the dream every day and everyone in my team knows this and has full faith in me!

What ranks and titles have you held? BJJ black belt, Ring of Combat middleweight champion.

Do you have any heroes? My younger brother Adam, and my HS wrestling coach Jay Nase. They’re both very big inspirations to me and I wouldn’t be where I am today without them.

Accomplishments in amateur competition? NJ State place winner in HS, Three-time Division I national qualifier, 2x Division I conference champion, 100 Division I career wins, and Male Athlete of the Year in 2004 for Rider University in wrestling.

Favorite striking technique: Ground and pound

Any accomplishments in amateur combat sports? Former Caged Aggression middleweight champ 

Any belts/ ranks in grappling disciplines? Purple belt in BJJ

What has been your toughest fight to date and why? Collin Huckbody, I fought him on the main event of Ignite last May. Physically the fight was easy, but mentally it was tough; he was 12-4 with a finish win on DWCS. I was 3-1 coming off a loss to a tough guy up in Canada. We were fighting on his home turf and the whole night was kind of a tribute to a teammate of his, Shaylee Lipp, who had passed away. Tensions were high and I knew he was motivated to win. But I ended up dominating him the whole fight and choked him out shortly before the end of round three. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Derrick Lewis, love watching him fight, like his style, love hearing him even more on the microphone.

Personal Life / Background: I grew up rural. I work a construction day job. I'm in the laborers union, pouring concrete from sunup to sundown.  I have a girlfriend of 12 years, Davita. We have three kids together, my oldest is my daughter, Raven Jane she is 6 and we share a birthday. Phoenix Rose is my middle child. She is 3. Lastly is my son Titan James, he's a year and half old. We have a small house out in the country, and enjoy gardening, hiking, longboard rides, river walks, shooting guns ... you know, s**t you do in the country. I'm a blue collar country boy, I want to put on for the people in this world who get  their hands dirty. 

I joined high school wresting my junior year and made the state finals my senior year. I owe the sport of wrestling, as well as my team and high school wrestling coach John Hatfield for unlocking a  hard work ethic and tenacious drive to be successful at everything I do.

Origin of nickname: “I was born and raised a blue-collar backwoods boy.”

TRAINING: A typical day of training for me is just like that I think of any other fighter: you wake up tired and sore and wanting to go back to bed instead of train, but somehow you get up and do it anyway...

When and why did you start training for fighting? I have always loved martial arts, but it was when I 15 years old and I watched my very first live kickboxing fights in Calgary that I had made the decision that fighting was what I wanted to do. The sport was so raw and savage (just like me) that I just had to try.  That was many years ago, but even to this day I love the feeling of competing and the weeks of preparation leading up to it - it gives my sad little life meaning knowing that I am working towards somebody else’s destruction. 

What ranks and titles have you held? I am a black belt Muay Thai under Mike Miles. 1998 - WKA Canadian Golden Gloves Super heavyweight Kickboxing Title. 1997 - WKA Canadian Super middleweight Kickboxing Title. 1998 - WKA Canadian Golden Gloves Super middleweight Kickboxing Title. 1999 - WKA Intercontinental Light heavyweight Muay Thai Title. 1999 - IAMTF World Amateur Muay Thai Championships - Bronze Medal. 2000 - NAMTC North American Light heavyweight MuayThai Title. I am a brown belt in Brazilian Jiu-jitsu under Roy Harris and trained in BJJ by Brian Bird. Bronze medalist at the 2008 Fila world grappling championships, 2 bronze medals at the 2009 Fila world grappling championships.

Do you have any heroes? Don Campbell of the Real Estate Investment Network - he seems like a man with a lot of integrity and I have looked up to him for years.  I have heard him speak many times and I don’t know why, but he puts me in a really good mood telling some very bad jokes.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? For me to have the opportunity to fight in the UFC is validation that my years of hard work to get to this point have finally paid off - It has been an uphill battle for me to get here.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I did do a few classes at university as an unclassified (part-time) student. I loved being in school and I did some chem/bio/psych classes.  I think that after that experience though it is safe to say that I am a better off using my muscles rather than my brains.  I’m pretty/not smart.

What was your job before you started fighting? I work at petrocanada pumping gas; they said that if I win this fight they will move me up to manager.
